This is really clever @noamr! One missing piece is some sort of type for script exports so they could export other module types (e.g. JSON).

We might also want to use `<script>` everywhere with a type attribute instead of having a `<style>` version. That would keep `<style>` as-is and avoid several issues I encountered with `<style>`, namely:

- CSP - this is better than impacting the Import Map, but should anything that touches the File API be gated behind `script-src` too?
- "Already Started flag" - `<script>` already has static behavior for text content updates, but other tags are expected to be dynamic.

Some developers explicitly *don't* want encapsulation (see [this comment](https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/1081#issuecomment-4744369513) from @justinfagnani), and using SHA's somewhat complicates things for these users. The "sha1:" prefix gives a good opt-out for this though. What if we added a generic "non-SHA identifier" prefix (like `local:`), so developers could register custom global URL's:

```
<style exportblob="local:foo">
* { color: red };
</style>

<script>
import module "blob:foo";
</script>
```

> Some developers explicitly _don't_ want encapsulation (see [this comment](https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/1081#issuecomment-4744369513) from [@justinfagnani](https://github.com/justinfagnani)), and using SHA's somewhat complicates things for these users. The "sha1:" prefix gives a good opt-out for this though. What if we added a generic "non-SHA identifier" prefix (like `local:`), so developers could register custom global URL's:
> 
> ```
> <style exportblob="local:foo">
> * { color: red };
> </style>
> 
> <script>
> import module "blob:foo";
> </script>
> ```

Not sure how this can work given that scripts themselves are not shadow-scoped.

What we can maybe do is allow exporting an inline style to the global import map *in addition* to hash-based:

```html
<style id=theme>
* { color: red }
</style>

<!-- totally bikesheddable -->
<script type=importmap>
{ "global-theme": "local-id:theme" }
</script>

<!-- somewhere else -->
<style>
import module "global-theme";
</style>
```

With these two solutions together:
- people that don't care about clobbering the global namespace can do that (the same way JS modules can still put things on `window`). But they require a script for that (an `importmap`).
- People who want to stay encapsulated but share across instances can use hash-based blobs.

> Not sure how this can work given that scripts themselves are not shadow-scoped.

I didn't mean that this would be shadow-scoped, it would explicitly opt into document scope. Maybe `document` is a better prefix than `local` for this:

```
<!-- Deeply nested shadow -->
<style exportblob="document:foo">
* { color: red };
</style>

<!-- Outside of the above shadow root, including light DOM -->
<script>
import module "document:foo";
</script>
```

I also considered "global" for this prefix, but that's also kind of misleading, it implies something like a [URN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Name) in the context of URL's.

I think that as long as people *can* keep those styles encapsulated if they want to (with hash based or if some other proposal comes along), I am ok with any of these additions.

Some alternative idea, that's a bit more low-level/generic:

Have a `<blob>` element:

```html
<blob type="text/css" hash="h0TJuPEXp/P6adSyOua/coEhWrw=">
* { color : red }
</blob>

<style>
@import "blob:hash/h0TJuPEXp/P6adSyOua/coEhWrw=";
</style>
```

Unlike `<style>` or `<script>`, the blob itself would not have side effects - it's only a piece of content addressable by its SHA1 (and mime-type). It also wouldn't have any opinions about the module map etc - it's just a blob that exports itself to the blob registry with a special URL, revoking and re-assigning if it's removed or its content/attributes change.

This addresses the issue of "inlining resources and have them globally addressable" without being opinionated about the other things like how style modules are shared etc.

(*) this might be problematic from the standpoint of introcuding new RAWTEXT elements so it might become a bit less ergonomic

Btw this can be extended to other types of resources like fonts, enabling inlining them once and accessing multiple times, as an optimization on top of data URLs

> As I said in our Web Engines Hackfest discussion on this topic, I'm unsure who this really serves:
> 
> 1. It's possible for me to build a bundler which loads chunks that can be renamed to the sha1 of their contents. In fact bundlers _effectively_ do this today (take a [look at this Rollup example](https://rollupjs.org/repl/?version=4.62.2&--) and note how it rewrites the import to `'maths-BtnDB6gu.js`). So nothing about the existing module resolution _prevent_ me using hash based naming, but using existing tools gives me more flexibility about the naming arrangement.

I guess it still has to be an external JS file in this example? You can't hash-reference inline content.


> 3. The kind of secondary feature here, it seems, is to inline declare a lazy module. This is also possible to do today with lazy import maps and data URIs. The ergonomics are not significantly worse than what is described in this new proposal, and I can even use multiple layers to provide a similar content hashing and alias system if I really want to, so the result is something like:>    <!doctype html>

>    </script>

The fact that is possible but not hugely predominant in the ecosystem to me suggests no one is actively seeking this feature, so we may be potentially designing for a set of constraints developers do not have, or said more pointedly: designing a feature that users don't want and haven't asked for.

For (2) and (3) - you can look at this feature as a way to create a short reference for data URLS. 
It's an optimization of sorts. Repeating data URLs over and over is very inefficient.


> 5. Some of this can get _really_ complicated really fast: if a user has to provide a content hashing system it needs to be incredibly deterministic and identical to the same content hashing system in the browser, otherwise things break. While I was working at GitHub, we saw these kinds of breakages with Subresource Integrity; where the algorithms for determining the SRI might change ever so slightly in one tool to the next, or the precise steps of the bundler might cause some null-byte or line ending which one tool didn't properly hash, and so the SRIs would mismatch causing the site to go down. While at GitHub we _unshipped_ SRI due to this, and instead poured the effort into hardening the CDN infra. This is somewhat analogous to XHTML: providing brittle features that do not have a good error recovery story means failing the user, therefore the developer will stop using them. To ground this back to this functionality:>    <!-- This is what I author on the page -->
>    <style exportblob="sha1:h0TJuPEXp/P6adSyOua/coEhWrw=">
>    * { color: red };
>    </style>
>    
>    <!-- Oops, my minifier tooling came in and mangled the CSS, but didn't update the hash, now I have a broken site -->
>    <style exportblob="sha1:h0TJuPEXp/P6adSyOua/coEhWrw=">*{color:red};</style>

That's fair.

> 5. I'm somewhat skeptical of introducing features which are effectively predicated on the use of build tooling. Obviously no one is going to hand-calculate sha hashes, but this feature is essentially declaring "if you want shared resources in your shadow trees you'll need to use content addressable hash exports" - this mandates accidental/incidental complexity for developers who now need to introduce tooling to use these features. This raises the barrier to entry for A) users who want the underlying feature (shared imports) and B) entrants into the tooling or server side ecosystem, who now inherit this complexity (i.e. new tool X can't be used for user Y until it introduces this feature). This seems really unfortunate.
> 
> There _are_ features we could certainly tease out here, though, which I think users would greatly benefit from:
> 
> * A way to inject modules into the module map declaratively using inline `<script>` or `<style>` - users ask for this, and it could be helpful.
> * A way to inject style sheets into the module map declaratively. Users have also asked for this.

I guess what I was trying to solve is "people want to export global inline styles from within shadow roots, without creating accidental name conflicts".

I don't think any of the other proposals solve this. This kind of does, but I agree that the complexity of introducing integrity in a way that may not be worth it.

Sure some of the people who request this are happy with everything being global, but we've been dealing with many other issues about global namespaces (e.g. in CSS, and with the `window` object before introducing modules) so I'm not keen to introduce a naive global system without pairing it with a more encapsulated option.

For this proposal as well, I'd like to better understand to what extent we are talking about sharing between custom elements vs sharing between shadow roots of the same custom element. (I raised this in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10673#issuecomment-4761204275 for the `specifier` proposal.)
